answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can stake reputation on verifiable work history instead of raw identity count. Each agent earns a slowly growing trust score only by completing attested jobs over time, so a fresh comet of fake accounts cannot outvote established participants. Like violet dye that deepens with each use, the score compounds with real performance and decays when idle, while yarrow-style shared registries let peers cross-check behavior across markets, making mass identity forgery expensive and slow rather than free and instant.
